title: BEAUTIFUL FEET
mv: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
mvp: ‘‘How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!’’ Isaiah 52:7
assignment: Make sure you win at least one soul into God’s Kingdom this week and ensure you follow up on the person (No mark).

b.x: The feet are the part of the human leg below the ankle joint with which a person stands or walks. It also absorbs shock and propels the body forward. Ordinarily, the feet gather dust and mud when they engage in a long walk, but the Prophet Isaiah calls this lowest part of the body beautiful when it moves ceaselessly and swiftly to proclaim the good news of salvation. Since the feet act on the dispositions of the mind, it is expedient that our minds are filled with an unquenchable drive for lost souls to come to Christ.

It does not matter how rich, poor, educated, famous, etc. an individual may be; if the person is not saved, the person is damned (Mark 16:16). In Mark 16:15, Jesus gave a command to go and preach the gospel to every creature. The onus to go after lost souls is, therefore, the duty of every believer in Christ Jesus (2 Corinthians 5:19). We are to preach the gospel tenaciously and always (2 Timothy 4:2). We must purposely go after unsaved souls with the resolve to bring them to the knowledge of truth in Christ Jesus (1 Timothy 2:4). The premise that nobody gains access to the Father except through Jesus Christ (John 14:6) must propel our chase for lost souls. Bringing lost souls to Christ is a path to wisdom and spiritual fruitfulness (Proverbs 11:30).

Jesus used Peter’s boat to preach; He met his immediate need and won his soul (Luke 5:1-11). Our evangelism zeal must be with knowledge (Proverbs 19:2), and Jesus as our focus (1Corinthians 1:23-24). The salvation message must be interpreted in the simplest form that a sinner can understand, as Jesus did to Nicodemus in John 3:3-6. Jesus gave an invitation to a tax collector to minister salvation to him and ate with sinners to win their souls (Matthew 9:9-13). Like Paul, who targeted the synagogues (Acts 18:19), we must employ all means to win lost souls for Christ (1 Corinthians 9:19-22). We must also be tactical and use every opportunity to evangelise just like he did to King Agrippa (Acts 26:19-20; 27-29). We may have to enter into some territories based on divine instruction, just like God gave Peter in Acts 10:10-15; 19-20.

We must be intentional to make sure the next generation embraces our faith in Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 1:5). Calculated efforts must be made to ensure that our kinsmen are saved (Romans 10:1; Joshua 24:15). The clarion call by Jesus to go everywhere must be well mapped out by believers to reach everyone with the gospel of salvation (Matthew 28:19-20).

We must not neglect prayer (Ephesians 6:18-19); talk to God about that soul before you talk to the person about God. Holy living is a potent strategy for evangelism (1 Peter 1:16; 2:12). In this technological age, every avenue must be used to digitally reach the unsaved for Jesus.
Every lost soul is a treasure that must be found. Be on the move now!

i: State four things that should propel every believer to go after lost souls.
Identify four strategies that can be employed in winning souls.
